verify.note: Three arms: (1) check:loom-integrity is a package script backed by a file with a vitest home, plus arm A and the primitive manifest; (2) lib/loom/store.ts writes loom_functions only through validateLoomFunction; (3) a surface under app/ reaches the store. Arm 1 passes since 2026-11-14; arms 2 and 3 need the loom_functions table.

append.detail: 2026-11-14 (first slice, dark): the Loom integrity gate is real, both arms, against real primitives and real schemas. SHIPPED: lib/loom/functions/primitives.ts is LOOM_PRIMITIVES, the one manifest (11 pure typed primitives over four kinds: text, number, boolean, list), each naming its module and export in lib/loom/functions/ops.ts. lib/loom/functions/validate.ts is arm A, validateLoomFunction(decl, ctx): pure, total, fail-closed, rules L1 to L8 (a real op; exactly the declared args, each of its kind; schema and field references resolved against the Zod SHAPE; acyclic, earlier-step-only, at most 24 steps; strict JSON data with no free identifiers or code; result kind equals the declared output; role floor on the ModuleRole ladder; every problem or the parsed function, never partial). No bypass. lib/loom/functions/context.ts derives the composable schemas from the adopted block contract (block:<type> is that block's own content schema, 45 today), never restated. lib/loom/functions/run.ts is the L9 read side, dark behind EDITOR_CANVAS (envFlag): it re-validates a stored declaration against today's manifest and schemas, so a retired primitive or a dropped field resolves to null and logs one line; it never throws and never writes. scripts/check-loom-integrity.mjs is arm B (M1 every primitive resolves to a real function export, ids unique, kinds are Loom kinds; M2 every schema is a Zod object; M3 the manifest is declared once; M4 .from('loom_functions') only in lib/loom/store.ts; M5 the store calls the validator, vacuous until the store exists; M6 arm A accepts a known-good declaration and rejects a broken one). It is the package script check:loom-integrity, enforced under vitest by scripts/check-loom-integrity.test.ts (named in guard-wiring.test.ts), which drives every arm against a broken copy. The old probe (the package script exists) now passes, so the verify moves to scripts/probes/editor/PROG-E9.mjs, which measures the whole consequence in three arms: arm 1 (this gate) passes, arms 2 and 3 fail. REMAINS, and why: (2) the store. lib/loom/store.ts needs a loom_functions table (declaration jsonb, scope, version, author, operator RLS), which is a migration; this slice wrote none by rule, so nothing can persist a declaration yet. (3) the operator surfaces: the declarative composer and the per-surface settings console under app/, which have nothing to save to until (2). Layer-2 config editing exists in part as app_overrides (enable, reorder, role floor per scope kind) at /admin/page-layout/apps; widening its key to (app_id, surface, space_id) per EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE §5 is also a migration. Not blocked by E2: the composer validates against the adopted block contract (E1), not a consolidated catalog. E2's usage index (block_type_usage, ADR-1502) counts placed blocks, not Loom functions, so retiring a primitive is still not reversible from CI; the gate's header says so.
